Programs

Four paths. One AI-native foundation.

Pick the outcome you want — insight, models, AI systems or autonomous agents. Every path is mapped session by session, and every one ends with work you can show.

01 / 04Bars → dashboards

Data Analyst with GenAI

3 Months · 60 sessions · 8 projects · Beginner-friendly

A 12-week, 60-session journey through the complete analyst toolkit: Advanced Excel and Power Query, SQL, Power BI with DAX, Python with Pandas, statistics, Generative AI for analytics, big-data foundations and your first machine-learning models.

  • Excel & Power Query
  • SQL

  • Python

  • Generative AI

Data Science with GenAI

6 Months · 120 sessions · 13 projects · Beginner to advanced

A 24-week, 120-session program that takes you from Python and statistics through machine learning, deep learning and computer vision, NLP and Generative AI, to SQL and Power BI — finishing with an end-to-end analytics system.

  • Python & Pandas

  • Machine Learning

  • NLP & GenAI
  • SQL & Power BI

03 / 04Layers → networks

Applied AI & Machine Learning

6 Months · 120 sessions · 7 projects · Intermediate to advanced

An engineering-grade, 120-session program: production Python, statistics and classical ML, deep learning and computer vision with TensorFlow, Transformers built from scratch, advanced RAG and agentic systems, fine-tuning and alignment — then DSA, SQL and MLOps with FastAPI and Docker.

  • Production Python
  • Classical ML
  • TensorFlow & Vision
  • Transformers
  • RAG & Agents
  • LoRA & RLHF
  • MLOps

AI Agents & Automation

6 Weeks · 36 sessions · 10 projects · No heavy coding required

A fast-paced 6-week, 36-session program: prompt engineering and APIs, MCP and agentic AI, no-code agents with Dify, n8n, CrewAI and Zapier, production RAG, AI UGC content factories, prompt-to-app development with Lovable, and production agents with OpenClaw.

How you’ll learn

Concept. Lab. Project. Proof.

01

Learn the concept

Every session opens with one focused idea — from conditional aggregation to attention mechanisms — explained from first principles.

02

Practise in a lab

Apply it immediately in Excel, notebooks, SQL editors, Power BI, TensorFlow or no-code agent builders.

03

Build a project

Combine skills into capstones that mirror real business problems: dashboards, models, RAG assistants, agents.

04

Show your proof

Publish to GitHub, present your capstones and walk into interviews with work that speaks for itself.

FAQ

Questions, answered.

Can’t find what you’re looking for? Message an advisor on WhatsApp — we’re happy to help.

Message an advisor
Which program should I choose?

Choose Data Analyst with GenAI (3 months) for dashboards, reporting and business insight; Data Science with GenAI (6 months) for the complete lifecycle from statistics to deep learning and GenAI; Applied AI & Machine Learning (6 months) for engineering-grade AI, LLMs and MLOps; or AI Agents & Automation (6 weeks) to build agents, automations and AI apps with little or no code. The program finder on our Programs page can help.

Do I need a technical background?

Not for most tracks. Data Analyst starts from Excel fundamentals and teaches Python from scratch; Data Science and Applied AI & ML both begin with Python foundations before moving into advanced material; AI Agents & Automation is largely no-code and low-code.

How is Generative AI part of every program?

Each curriculum includes dedicated GenAI content: LLMs and prompt engineering for analytics, OpenAI/Gemini/LLaMA apps and LangChain RAG for data science, Transformers from scratch, advanced RAG, fine-tuning and agents for applied AI, and an entire program built around agents and automation.

Will I build real projects?

Yes — 38 projects and capstones across the four programs, from executive Power BI reports and YOLO object detection to RAG assistants, multi-agent systems and production AI agents.

Can I see the full curriculum before I apply?

Absolutely. Every program page includes a searchable, day-by-day curriculum, and each one has a downloadable PDF brochure.

How do I apply?

Use the Apply page to choose your program and share a few details. An admissions advisor will then contact you to discuss fit, schedules and next steps.
